STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of fish fillets (salmon-like, pink flesh) topped with a green herb and cream/mash-like coating, on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly top-down, so the plate is seen close to true shape.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 26 cm across its width. Area ≈ 26 x 26 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 575 cm^2; using a round-equivalent, about 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) Salmon-type fish fillet pieces, three portions, one with skin visible; (2) a pale green herb-crumb/cream topping over the fish; (3) small herb leaves (basil-like) scattered on top.

STEP 4 - Area: Fish pieces cover ~30% of the plate (upper piece ~10%, middle-right ~10%, lower-left ~10%). Topping is part of the same pieces, so counted together. Herb leaves ~1%. Total covered ≈ 31%, roughly 165 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: Fish with topping, average height ~1.8 cm. 165 cm^2 x 1.8 cm ≈ 300 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Dense fish/topping mix at 0.95 g/ml ≈ 285 g. Split: fish fillet ~230 g, herb crumb/cream topping ~50 g, herb leaves ~2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy (cooked, as plated):
- Salmon fillet, cooked: ~200 kcal/100 g → 230 g = 460 kcal
- Crumb/cream topping (mixed, moderate fat): ~250 kcal/100 g → 50 g = 125 kcal
- Basil leaves: ~25 kcal/100 g → 2 g = 0.5 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three fish portions with topping on a large plate, about 280 g total, is plausible. Total ≈ 585 kcal.
